build.name: Blend
build.why: bundle has it; two sketches to a tapered solid
build.label: Loft
build.landed: 2026-09-01 gauntlet round 10. A BlendFeature taking exactly two sketches, emitted as a generated blendOnPlane() helper built on extrudeFromSlices with two slices -- the smallest real loft. It takes no numbers of its own on purpose: the two sketches already say which plane they sit on and how far along it they are, so the gap IS the difference in their offsets and the solid starts at the lower one. A height field would be a third number that could disagree with two that were already true. Both corner lists are emitted as PARAMETERS, so dragging a corner still reshapes the solid. Refuses, with a sentence naming the fix, when the two sketches sit on different planes, at the same offset, or when either is not a sketch. Measured in the gate against the frustum formula (40x40 to 10x10 over 30 = 21000 cubic units, within 2%), plus the two cases the helper exists for: a 4-corner outline blended to a 6-corner one, and one outline drawn the opposite way round building the SAME solid rather than a bow tie.
build.note: Two deliberate simplifications, both visible rather than hidden. Both outlines are walked from their OWN first corner, so a shape rotated relative to the other blends with a twist -- predictable beats clever, since untwisting means searching for an alignment a student cannot see the reason for. And two slices means the sides are straight; Onshape's Loft can take guide curves and more than two profiles, which this does not. Building it also closed a latent trap in labelOf(): the chain ended in a bare `: 'Sphere'`, so the first blend built correctly and called itself 'Sphere 1'. The tail is now exhaustive against `never`, so the next new feature kind fails to compile rather than quietly inheriting a name.

build.name: Surface
build.why: plane already in the model as xy/xz/yz+offset but no toolbar affordance
build.label: Plane
build.landed: 2026-09-01 gauntlet round 9. The third instance of the same shape as Arc and the bulge writer: newSketch(doc, plane) has always taken a plane, SketchFeature has always carried one, extrudeOnPlane() has always built on all three, and model-codegen-assertions.cjs has pinned xz and yz since the first sketch build -- and the single caller passed nothing, so every sketch in the app was born on xy and could never leave. What landed is a 'Sits on:' row at the top of the Rules panel (Ground / Front / Side, with the real xy/xz/yz name in each tooltip, the same bargain the Mirror flyout already strikes) wired through setSketchPlane() in ModelEditor.tsx. Moving a sketch does not touch its own coordinates, so the outline, rules, rounds, chamfers and bows all come with it. Verified live including that the shape really reorients in space rather than only in the panel.
build.note: It also closed a hole found while building it: SketchConstraints was mounted only for non-circle sketches, so a circle got no panel and therefore no way to leave the ground. A circle now reaches the panel and gets the plane row ALONE -- it has no edges to rule and no corners to pin. Onshape's Plane feature creates a free datum plane at an arbitrary angle; that is not this. Ours is the three principal planes plus the offset slider the Dimensions panel already had, which is what a sketch here can actually sit on.

build.why: BUILT AND MEASURED in lib/occt-build.ts, 2026-09-01, not yet reachable from the toolbar. One NAMED edge is rounded or bevelled -- the edge is named as the meeting of two named faces (the `between` cause in lib/topo-name.ts), so it survives a rebuild. Checked against arithmetic rather than a golden number: a fillet of radius r along an edge of length L removes exactly (1 - pi/4) * r^2 * L, on a 40x30x20 box and again on a 70x12x46 one, where the same name finds the same edge and the loss follows the new length. What ships today is JSCAD roundRadius, which rounds every edge of a box at once and cannot be pointed at one. REMAINING: the preview still runs JSCAD, so the feature passes its target through unchanged there -- see whyNotOnJscad() in lib/model-types.ts -- and no toolbar button creates one yet.

BUILT AND MEASURED in lib/occt-build.ts, 2026-09-01, not yet reachable from the toolbar. BRepOffsetAPI_DraftAngle on a named face, with the pull direction and neutral plane stored on the feature because neither has a defensible default. Body Draft is every face except the two the pull points at -- exact for the axis-aligned primitives, rougher than Onshape on a shape whose sides are not parallel to the pull, which is stated on DraftFeature rather than discovered. REMAINING: same as fillet-edge -- preview engine and a toolbar affordance.

NOT kernel-blocked, which the old refusal got wrong. BRepAlgoAPI_Section is bound and returns the section edges; a cut-by-halfspace twice gives both halves. The real blocker is ModelDoc: a Split produces TWO bodies from one, and every feature kind here maps one id to one shape. BOPAlgo_Splitter, which would do it in one call, is absent from this build. Queued behind deciding how a document names a second body, which is a document design question and not a geometry one.

NOT kernel-blocked either, and never was. A rib is a recipe, not an API: pull a sketch line into a thin wall, keep only the part inside the body, fuse it on. Every step of that already exists here -- extrude, intersect, union. Queued on the UI question of drawing a rib line against an existing solid, which the sketch surface has no affordance for yet.

tools: Sheet Metal Table and Flat View
outOfScope.why: a manufacturing discipline with its own vocabulary; no JSCAD kernel support and nothing in a first-year CS course reaches for it MEASURED COST OF LIFTING THIS (2026-09-01): the only browser B-rep kernel is OpenCascade compiled to wasm (replicad-opencascadejs), which is 21.9 MB and LGPL-2.1-only. reSHape ships on JSCAD today at 0.41 MB total for modeling, renderer and io, all MIT -- so this is 53x the payload for every student on every preview load, plus an LGPL kernel inside an otherwise-MIT app that has already been extracted as MIT public repos. Across all four kernel-blocked groups it buys 34 tools, of which 28 are sheet metal and surfacing this file already refuses on pedagogy. REFUSED on cost, not on ignorance. Revisit only if the course needs Draft or Thread specifically, or if a custom OCCT build trimmed to the modules reSHape uses lands under a couple of MB. REVERSED 2026-09-01, same day: the refusal above weighed B-rep only by which toolbar entries it unlocks, which is the wrong measure. The stated goal is a true PARAMETRIC modeller with persistent face and edge references, and that is not a feature list -- it is a representation. A mesh has no face to refer to, which is why Bevel on a cylinder is a hull of two cylinders rather than a chamfer. Two numbers were also overstated: 21.9 MB is the uncompressed wasm, it is 6.9 MB gzipped and cached after first load, and the runner is already conditional on lesson.preview === "reshape" rather than loading everywhere. LGPL for a wasm module loaded at runtime is the case LGPL was written for and does not reach our own code. These tools are QUEUED behind the parametric core, not refused.

no extrudeAlongPath in the vendored bundle; extrudePath exists but is unexposed and untested. Reconsider if a lesson needs it

External Thread needs a helix to sweep a profile along. Measured in the OpenCascade build reSHape now targets (2026-09-01): no Helix, no extrudeHelical, and BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell has no path to ride -- the whole Curve tools group is refused for the same missing piece. This is a narrower refusal than the one it replaces: the old reason was "needs face or edge selection on a B-rep", which is no longer true of anything here. Onshape's own External Thread is largely an annotation rather than cut geometry, so a cosmetic version is reachable without a helix and is a deliberate non-goal for a first-year course, not a gap.
